protocol.description:
Lets a client describe where the compositor draws its background effect (blur) behind a surface as a list of rounded rectangles, each with its own opacity and material, instead of the rectangles of a wl_region.
This complements ext_background_effect_v1: a surface with blur shapes is treated as a surface that set a blur region, so blur is on unless the compositor's rules say otherwise, and the shapes take the place of the region.

interface.name: niri_blur_shapes_manager_v1
interface.description: On bind, the compositor sends one material event per material it can draw. Material 0, plain blur, is always available and not announced.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the surface already has a blur shapes object

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created through this manager are not affected.

request.name: get_blur_shapes

description.summary: get the blur shapes object for a surface

request.description: It is a protocol error to ask for a second object for the same surface while the first exists.

event.name: material

description.summary: a material the compositor can draw

event.description: A named look for the blurred background, configured in the compositor. Sent on bind and again, for every material, when the configuration changes; an id is only meaningful until the next done event.

interface.name: niri_blur_shapes_v1
interface.description: The shapes are double-buffered state, applied on the next wl_surface.commit. Once reset, the committed list replaces the surface's ext_background_effect_v1 blur region; an empty list means no blur.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: go back to the blur region

request.description: On the next commit the surface's blur region applies again.

request.name: reset
request.description: Empties the pending list of shapes.

request.name: add_rounded_rect

description.summary: add a shape to the pending list

request.description:
Coordinates are in the surface-local coordinate space. Radii larger than half the shorter side are reduced to fit. The alpha multiplies the whole effect inside the shape and is clamped to 0..1.
A material id the compositor did not announce draws plain blur. The tint is a colour laid over the blurred background in the shape, premultiplied 0xRRGGBBAA; a material may ignore it, and 0 means none.

event.name: backdrop

description.summary: how bright the backdrop behind a shape is

event.description:
The mean luminance of the blurred background behind a shape, from 0 (black) to 1 (white), so the client can draw what's on it light or dark to suit.
Sent only for shapes whose material the compositor configured to report it, and only where it measures the background itself (not for see-through, xray, effects). The reading is coarse and late: it is taken at most a few times a second, and sent when it moved noticeably since the last one sent for that shape. The index is the shape's place, from 0, in the list of the commit it was drawn for; a client should ignore an index past its current list.
